validator: passes with no problems (with --case); case.json validates

faults.finding: 'Each one means the conductor reaches its maximum temperature at a lower current' is asserted, not shown. The step that makes it obvious: a warm room starts the conductor warmer, and neighbouring circuits or insulation stop it shedding its heat, so less current takes it to its limit.
faults.fix: Add that step in one clause before 'so the cable can carry less there'.

faults.finding: 'Ca everywhere' reads as one ambient for the whole run; the ambient is present everywhere, but a run through a hotter plant room has a different Ca there.
faults.fix: Say 'Ca for the ambient of each part'.

faults.finding: The source says a BS 3036 fuse's I2 can be up to 2 × Iz, that is, when its rating is matched to the cable's Iz; the draft says 'up to twice' as if of In without saying so. And the maker's 1 hour is quoted for its type C and D breakers, while the slides' example is type B.
faults.fix: Say 'up to twice, with its rating matched to the cable' and 'for its type C and D breakers up to 63 A'.

faults.fault: practice value not labelled where it appears
faults.finding: 16.66 A and 1.5 mm² rest on the practice Ca of 1.00; the explanation prints them without saying so.
faults.fix: Add 'with Ca taken as 1.00, a practice value'.

faults.finding: Three section names such as 'Through the insulated wall' in a third of a phone's width will wrap to three lines over the drawing.
faults.fix: Short names on the drawing (Clipped, Trunking, Insulated wall), the full ones in the working under it.

faults.finding: 'Counted as two circuits' cites the Table 4C1 note that allows n/2 or n/3; the n/3 reading for three-phase circuits is the On-Site Guide's.
It names the cable's mark rising but not why: Cf raises the Iz the cable needs.
faults.fix: Name it as the Iz needed rising to 13.79 A, within 40 words.

Twelve screens. No timers, marks or grades.
No recall-only checks: read mode, checks []; the screen 5 check applies Table 4C1 note 9 and 'Cg counts the circuit itself' to new numbers.

Practice values labelled wherever they appear: Ca 1.00 at 20 °C (p.Ca) on screen 8, in practice and the case; the 2.7 star start (p.start) on screen 7. No BS 7671 table reproduced: only the single values each question needs (Cg 0.80 and 0.70, Ca 1.02, 15 A and 20 A in column 5), each quoted from his copy, and 'read column 5 in your copy'.
Lesson 1 not re-taught: Ib and the delta winding current are carried forward, not worked again.

The slides' '10,000s' (p.30) is said as the slides say it, beside a maker's 1 hour, and the check I2 ≤ 1.45 Iz is shown not to depend on it, as case.json's caution asks.
